issues.description: Unbounded log buffer can balloon memory if session never starts cleanly
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer is a plain list that accumulates every root logger record until init_recording or cleanup runs. A job that hangs early (e.g. stuck in connect retry loops emitting frequent logs) could grow this buffer unboundedly. Consider a maxlen deque or byte cap with drop policy.

issues.description: Removing all LoggingHandlers during shutdown may strip user-installed OTLP handlers
issues.detail: _shutdown_telemetry now iterates root.handlers and removes any opentelemetry LoggingHandler instance. If a user attached their own OTLP LoggingHandler (separate logger provider) it will be silently detached. Scope removal to the handler this module installed, or track it explicitly.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer replays records through only the first matching OTLP handler
issues.detail: The loop breaks after the first LoggingHandler found, but _setup_cloud_tracer may install via a specific logger_provider; if other LoggingHandler instances exist, replay may target the wrong one. Also, replaying via handler.emit bypasses level/filter checks that propagate() would apply, possibly duplicating logs already captured.

issues.description: _on_cleanup calls init_recording which triggers heavy cloud tracer setup on crash path
issues.detail: When a job crashes before session.start, _on_cleanup now calls init_recording(logs=True), which invokes _setup_cloud_tracer synchronously inside a cleanup hook. This adds network/SDK setup during teardown and could itself raise or hang; the bare except logs but _stop_log_buffering only runs on failure, not on partial success.

issues.description: Test parallelism disabled and test_plugin_google_stt removed without explanation
issues.detail: makefile drops `-n auto` from pytest and removes tests/test_plugin_google_stt.py from the unit suite. This will materially slow CI and reduces coverage with no comment in the PR description explaining why. If these are temporary workarounds they need a tracking issue.

issues.description: Race in _on_entry_done forcing shutdown_fut may suppress legitimate shutdown path
issues.detail: Setting _shutdown_fut from the done callback with InvalidStateError suppression means a normal shutdown that already set the future is silently masked, but the error log still fires. Consider also logging the forced-shutdown only when set_result actually succeeded so logs reflect real state transitions.

review.summary: The PR adds crash-log buffering and replay to ensure logs upload when a session crashes before init_recording. The mechanism is reasonable but the buffer is unbounded, the OTLP handler removal during shutdown is too aggressive, and the cleanup-time init_recording call introduces heavy teardown work that can mask new failures. Unrelated test changes (disabling -n auto, dropping a google STT test) need justification. Worth tightening before merge.
